title: ARIA, screen readers and alternative text

videos.script:
A screen reader does not read the screen. {{tree}} It reads a tree the browser builds from the HTML: for every element, a role, a name and a state. If the tree is wrong, the person hears something wrong, however good the page looks.

So today we print the planner's tree, and read it as a listener would. {{names}} The back link is called by the name of an arrow. There is no main region to jump to. And adding a session changes the page in silence.

Three fixes, each with a test first. {{fixes}} A link that says where it goes. A main landmark. And a status line that is read out when a session is added.

Then the rule that keeps all this small: if HTML has an element for the job, use it. {{aria}} The whole planner needs two ARIA attributes.

Images get alt text by deciding what they are for. {{alt}} And at the end, you turn on a real screen reader and listen.
